headline: Trade is mutual exchange—giving what you have to get what you need
universal_truth: Exchange creates value; both sides gain when trade is voluntary and fair
fun_facts: Trade has existed for at least 150,000 years—it's deeply human
Long-distance trade networks existed in ancient times across continents
Specialization and trade together explain much of human prosperity
discussion_questions: What do you trade—goods, services, time?
When does trade feel fair and when does it feel exploitative?
How has trade shaped your life?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: You have something I want. I have something you want. Trade solves this—we each give what we have less need for and get what we need more. This simple exchange is foundation of economy.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: Why not just make everything yourself? Why depend on others through trade?

options.text: Trade enables specialization—instead of everyone doing everything poorly, people get good at specific things; through exchange, everyone accesses what others do best; trade multiplies capability
options.response: Yes. You can't be expert at everything. Trade lets you focus on what you do best and access others' expertise. This division of labor is why economies produce more than individuals could alone.

options.text: Trade is just about getting stuff
options.response: Getting things is the surface, but trade enables the entire structure of specialized, productive society...

q1.title: Value Creation
q1.script: Trade creates value. Before exchange, each person has something they value less. After, each has something they value more. Both sides gain—that's why voluntary trade happens.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Value Creation"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Trust Required
q2.script: Trade requires trust. Will you deliver what you promised? Will I pay? Trade works when people trust each other. Contracts, laws, and reputation systems all support trading trust.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Fair Exchange
q3.script: Not all trades are equal. Power imbalances can make exchanges exploitative. Fair trade means both parties have options and information. Unfair trade is one-sided extraction.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Exchange creates value. Both sides gain when trade is voluntary and fair. Participate in and honor fair exchange.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 337. Tomorrow, we'll explore how money works—the tool that makes trade easier. Until then, notice how trade structures your daily life.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Trade Mapping - What Do You Exchange?
growTrack.activity: Map the trades in your life: What do you give (work, money, goods)? What do you receive? Which trades feel fair? Which feel unequal? How might you improve the terms of your exchanges?
